title: Meeting Rooms
summary: Find the fewest rooms that can host every meeting without two meetings sharing a room at once.
statement:
An office manager is booking rooms for tomorrow's `n` meetings. Meeting `i` needs a room from time `start[i]` up to, but not including, time `end[i]`: the half-open interval `[start[i], end[i])`.

A room can host only one meeting at a time. Because the intervals are half-open, a meeting that ends at time `t` frees its room in time for another meeting that starts at time `t`.

Find the minimum number of rooms needed so that every meeting has a room for its whole duration.
functionDescription:
Complete the **minMeetingRooms** function in the editor below.

**minMeetingRooms** has the following parameter:

- `int meetings[n][2]`: each row holds the `start` and `end` time of one meeting

**Returns**

- `int`: the minimum number of rooms needed
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer, `n`, the number of meetings.

Each of the next `n` lines contains two space-separated integers, `start[i]` and `end[i]`.
outputFormat: Print the minimum number of rooms as a single integer.

samples.explanation: `[1, 4)` and `[2, 6)` overlap, so one room is not enough. Two rooms work: the first hosts `[1, 4)`, `[4, 7)` and `[8, 10)`, and the second hosts `[2, 6)` and `[6, 9)`. Each meeting that starts exactly when another ends can reuse its room.
At time `3`, the meetings `[0, 10)`, `[2, 5)` and `[3, 8)` are all in progress, so at least `3` rooms are needed. `[5, 6)` starts when `[2, 5)` ends and can take its room, so `3` rooms are enough.
